handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, decided, or built in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

major_misses.root_cause: Our formula assumes stockpile ($2.81/CY). Solara specifies haul-off to waste — 6-7x more expensive. These are fundamentally different scope items. Need a Gemini flag: strip_haul_off_required.

Ballast rule fired because typical section mentions base course. But Solara's paving is 2/6" (6" base bundled in unit price, not a separate pay item). Rule needs to gate on whether ballast is an explicit separate bid item vs bundled in paving spec.

major_misses.note: STRIP LOTS $61,100 + LOT EXC TO EMBANK PH5 $55,500 + PLACE TOPSOIL $30,450 + STRIP LOTS PH5 $25,000. Lot pad prep items — not in our model at all. Appear on larger developer-prep subdivisions. Need Gemini flag: lot_grading_in_scope.

major_misses.root_cause: Larger subdivisions sometimes require 12" transmission main in addition to 8" distribution. Not in our model. Need Gemini flag: large_diameter_water_main_present.
Even the large export tier ($38k+) is 3x too low for 10,000 CY. The tier needs CY-based scaling, not just a floor.
Swales is non-linear with ROW_SF. Small jobs: $0.19-0.30/ROW_SF. Solara: $0.56/ROW_SF. ROW_SF scaling assumption breaks on large jobs.

Solara is the portfolio outlier ($103,500 vs typical $12-15k). Likely includes community signage package + crosswalk beacon systems. High-variance item (CV > 1.0) — cannot be reliably estimated from analogs.

major_misses.note: 65-67% of actual across all types. ROW_SF scaling does not extrapolate well from small analogs to large jobs.

architecture_decision.problem: Hard-coded thresholds and rules in the system prompt do not scale. When you add more jobs, the rules need to be re-derived manually. The system needs to self-update.
architecture_decision.agreed_solution: Move all statistical findings out of the system prompt and into the knowledge pack (computed by derive_patterns.py). System prompt describes methodology only. LLM reads statistical thresholds from the knowledge pack at inference time. When a job is added, run derive_patterns.py — everything updates automatically.

architecture_decision.key_principle: System prompt = HOW to use statistics. Knowledge pack = THE statistics. Numbers never live in the system prompt.

implementation_plan.overview: Three parallel work streams. Do them in order — each depends on the previous.

stream_1_derive_patterns_extension.goal: Add three new top-level sections to knowledge_pack.json output

section_1_item_prevalence.description: For every distinct line item description in the portfolio, compute prevalence stats and conditional prevalence by job-level buckets.

EXAMPLE_ITEM.jobs_present: int — how many jobs include this item

implementation_notes: Normalize item descriptions before comparison (lowercase, strip trailing spaces/punctuation) to avoid duplicates
Thresholds for conditional buckets: ROW_SF split at 130,000 SF (separates Lone Fir/Settlement/Solara from small jobs); lot_count split at 35 (separates Solara from others)
These thresholds are hard-coded in derive_patterns.py as named constants so they can be updated as portfolio grows
When portfolio grows beyond ~20 jobs, these thresholds should be recomputed as actual percentiles (median ROW_SF etc.) rather than fixed values — add a TODO comment for this

section_2_ls_item_variance.description: For LS (lump sum) line items, compute coefficient of variation across jobs that include the item. High CV = high uncertainty = Claude should flag and widen confidence band.

EXAMPLE_LS_ITEM.n: int — number of jobs with this item

per_ROW_SF.note: string — e.g. 'moderate — scaling unreliable above 130k ROW_SF'

section_2_ls_item_variance.which_items: Any line item with unit=LS and n>=3. Key ones: SWALES, EXC TO EMBANK, DEMO, SIGNS & STRIPING, TRAFFIC CONTROL, MOBILIZATION, STRIP ROW.
section_2_ls_item_variance.cv_thresholds_for_system_prompt: CV < 0.3 = low variance (scale confidently); CV 0.3-0.7 = moderate (scale with caution, flag); CV > 0.7 = high variance (do not rely on analog scaling — flag as ±40%+ uncertainty)

section_3_item_scaling.description: For measurable (non-LS) line items, compute OLS regression against the top candidate drivers and report best-fit formula. This replaces hard-coded formulas in the system prompt.

EXAMPLE_MEASURABLE_ITEM.slope: float — qty per unit of driver
EXAMPLE_MEASURABLE_ITEM.secondary_driver: string — second best if r2 within 0.05 of best

implementation_notes: Exclude Phase 2 jobs (forest_grove_ph2) from all regressions — they're outliers
Minimum n=3 for any regression; report null slopes for items with n<3
For items where lot_count rule gives r2=1.0 (SEWER SERVICES, WATER SERVICES, IRRIGATION SLEEVES), still include them here but note as 'derivation rule'
Run regression for all three drivers, pick the one with highest r2

stream_2_new_gemini_flags.goal: Add 4 new boolean extraction fields that gate the 4 structural problem items

fields_to_add.gemini_guidance: Set true ONLY if the spec sheet or quantity notes list ballast or crushed aggregate base as a SEPARATE bid item with its own pay quantity (e.g., '12" BALLAST', 'CRUSHED AGGREGATE BASE COURSE'). Set false if the base course is described as part of the paving spec (e.g., '2/4" paving' or '3/6" paving' — the '/4' or '/6' denotes the base thickness bundled into the paving unit price). The distinction is: is there a separate line item for base rock, or is it folded into the paving price?
fields_to_add.system_prompt_change: Change ballast rule from 'include if typical section mentions ballast' to 'include only if ballast_is_separate_pay_item = true'. This fixes the $176k Solara false positive.

fields_to_add.gemini_guidance: Set true if the stripping or clearing notes specify material must be hauled off-site to a waste or disposal area. Look for: 'INCL HAUL OFF', 'haul to waste', 'haul to off-site disposal', 'remove and dispose', 'export to waste site'. Set false if notes say 'stockpile', 'stockpile on-site', 'spread and compact', or no disposal instruction is given (default = stockpile). This distinction is critical for pricing — haul-off stripping costs 6-8x more than stockpile stripping.
fields_to_add.system_prompt_change: Add a strip haul-off rate tier. If strip_haul_off_required=true, use LS item priced from haul-off analogs (Solara: $178,000 for 8,813 CY = ~$20/CY). If false, use existing stockpile formula ($2.81/CY median).

fields_to_add.gemini_guidance: Set true if the plans include work on the individual lots beyond the road ROW. Look for: grading plans that extend into lot interiors, notes like 'strip lots', 'lot grading', 'rough grade lots', 'place topsoil on lots', 'lot excavation', 'import fill to lots'. Set false if grading work is confined to the road ROW and utility corridors only.
fields_to_add.system_prompt_change: If lot_grading_in_scope=true, include LOT PREP EARTHWORK as a separate LS item. Pricing: scale from analogs that include lot prep; flag as high-uncertainty LS item. Killdeer/Woodman have lot_grading_in_scope=false and are unaffected.

fields_to_add.gemini_guidance: Set true if the utility plan shows a water main larger than 8" diameter (10", 12", or larger) in addition to or instead of the standard 8" distribution main. These are typically transmission mains required for larger subdivisions or fire flow. Look for: '10" WATER MAIN', '12" WATER MAIN PVC', large-diameter pipe shown on the utility plan with a separate symbol/label from the 8" distribution lines.
fields_to_add.system_prompt_change: If large_diameter_water_main_present=true, include a separate large-diameter water main line item. Pricing from the 1-2 analogs that have it (Solara: 592 LF of 12" @ $146.75 = $86,876). Quantity from ROW_SF scaling against those analogs. Flag as thin data.

stream_2_new_gemini_flags.also_add_to_sidecar: Add all 4 new fields to the Scope Flags table in the .gemini_extraction.md sidecar (already has demo_scope_present and irrigation_service_present — extend that table).

stream_3_system_prompt_methodology_shift.goal: Replace hard-coded numbers with references to knowledge pack fields. Do NOT rewrite the whole prompt — make surgical replacements.

specific_changes.what: Scaling formulas (rolled curb LF, sidewalk SF, scupper EA, etc.)
specific_changes.to: Knowledge pack reference: 'ROLLED CURB: use item_scaling.ROLLED_CURB.formula from knowledge pack (currently road_LF × 1.43, r2=0.999)'
specific_changes.why: When more jobs are added, derive_patterns.py updates the slope automatically

specific_changes.what: Item inclusion logic for prevalence-driven items
specific_changes.from: Hard-coded: 'Include BALLAST if any of 2 closest analogs include it'
specific_changes.to: Knowledge pack + flag: 'Include BALLAST if ballast_is_separate_pay_item=true (from Gemini) AND item_prevalence.BALLAST.prevalence > 0.2'
specific_changes.why: Prevalence gate + Gemini flag together prevent false positives

specific_changes.to: Read ls_item_variance.CV from knowledge pack. If CV > 0.7, flag as high-uncertainty and state ±40% on that line item. If CV > 1.0 (SIGNS & STRIPING), state that analog scaling is unreliable and use the portfolio median with explicit high-uncertainty flag.

specific_changes.what: Large-job items (12" water main, lot prep)
specific_changes.to: Add rules gated on new Gemini flags, using item_prevalence conditional stats to confirm inclusion logic

do_not_change: The lot_count derivation rules for sewer/water services (r2=1.0, n=9+, these work perfectly)
The analog selection methodology (ROW_SF primary, lot_count secondary)
The earthwork tier structure (keep the tiers, just add CY-based scaling for large export)
The co-occurrence rules (already in knowledge pack)

EXC TO EMBANK: Gemini classified Killdeer as roughly_balanced but actual has confirmed import ($38k). Needs a skepticism/validation mechanism — possibly ask Claude to cross-check Gemini's earthwork_balance against the profile grade delta described in earthwork_notes.

SWALES non-linearity: $0.19-0.30/ROW_SF for small jobs vs $0.56/ROW_SF for Solara. The ls_item_variance regression will expose this. May need a breakpoint model or a lot_count driver instead of ROW_SF for large jobs.
